question: When magnetic field is acting towards north and current is moving in east to west direction through a conductor, then the conductor will move ______ direction
solution:
The correct answer is __**in the downward**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a magnetic field is acting towards the north and the current is moving from east to west through a conductor, the conductor will experience a force due to the interaction of the magnetic field and the current.
 
• This phenomenon is explained by the **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**, which helps determine the direction of the force acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
 
• According to Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, if you align your left hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current (east to west), the forefinger pointing in the direction of the magnetic field (north), then the middle finger will point in the direction of the force (downward).
 
• Therefore, the conductor will move in the **downward direction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule** is a visual mnemonic used in physics to predict the direction of the force exerted on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
 
• The rule states that if you hold your left hand with the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger mutually perpendicular to each other, with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current, the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, the middle finger will point in the direction of the force or motion.
 
• This principle is crucial in the functioning of electric motors, where the interaction between the magnetic field and the current produces motion.
 
• Understanding the direction of forces in magnetic fields is essential for designing and operating various electrical devices and systems.
